items.title: Run full iOS 16.5 firmware on Android Devices
items.content:
HackiOS boots Apple's open-source XNU kernel ( xnu-8796.121.2 , the kernel of iOS 16.5) on Android phone

hardware and runs the unmodified iOS 16.5 user space on top of it: launchd → backboardd → SpringBoard →

apps. Our own EFI loader, our own replacements for Apple's closed drivers, a UEFI port, and a Linux Wi-Fi driver

on a compatibility layer make that possible.

POCO X5 Pro 5G (redwood, Snapdragon 778G) — nothing is flashed: the UEFI is started with fastboot boot ,

the whole system lives in RAM, and after a reboot the phone is back in Android;

QEMU ( virt , aarch64) — the same thing on any Linux computer, no phone needed.

XNU patches, the EFI loader, the UEFI port, Wi-Fi, QEMU scripts, xl , prebuilt kernel/loader/UEFI, common/ scripts

our init, injected libraries, launchd jobs, the APFS image builder, the scripts that take iOS out of Apple's IPSW, Metal/Mesa work

No Apple files are in either repository. ios165/fetch.sh downloads the iOS 16.5 IPSW from Apple's own CDN

to your machine and extracts what is needed there. HackiOS is an independent research project by OOSEX GANG and

is not affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by Apple Inc. iOS, iPhone and Apple are trademarks of Apple Inc.

Photographed on the phone, the Adreno GPU drawing ( gpu=1 ). More in Screenshots .

Lock screen, swipe to unlock, home screen with all icons (two pages), stock iOS 16 wallpapers

System gestures: swipe up (home, app switcher), edge swipe (back), Control Center

Charging under our kernel (the phone only discharges)

Apps: Settings, Clock, Calendar, Photos, Notes, Safari and more; widgets (Weather, Calendar) on the phone

Metal for apps (in progress: 293 of 456 system shaders already run on the Adreno, see docs/air.md in hackios-xnu-userland)

Phone touchscreen (Goodix GT9916), multitouch, wake on touch; real power and volume keys

App Store content and Apple ID sign-in (no Secure Enclave; FairPlay daemon exits)

Up to 8 CPU cores ( cpus=8 ), big core at 2.4 GHz, ~20 s to the lock screen

Adreno 642L GPU through Mesa/freedreno ( gpu=1 , OpenGL ES for CoreAnimation)

Wi-Fi (WCN6750, ath11k): join from Settings, Safari over Wi-Fi, 55–90 Mbit/s

Sound (speakers, main microphone), camera in Camera.app (front/rear, preview, focus, HEIC photos)

Data that iOS writes survives a reboot ( var_store=1 ufs_write=1 ); iOS root volume on the phone's flash

Sileo + Procursus (dpkg, apt), tweaks, SSH

It is a research bench, not a ROM: a session lasts a given number of seconds, then the kernel returns to the

prebuilt/ holds the kernel, loader and our programs built from these repositories, so all you need is the system

image, which is made on your machine from Apple's IPSW.

Needs: Linux x86-64, ~12 GB free disk, 4 GB free RAM. Packages (Arch):

sudo pacman -S --needed git python 7zip lz4 gcc qemu-system-aarch64 qemu-ui-gtk edk2-aarch64

Keys: H home, L lock/power, ↑ / ↓ volume, F11 (hold) five fingers.

This feature allows you to register multiple mappings in order to load

local files through custom https:// URLs.

This prevents having to spawn a HTTP server to test a web page.

This makes it easy to test all Web APIs, including the ones being restricted

This also helps having many distinct origins (domain) for each experiment / project

and have dedicated storage/cookies for each.

These mappings are only accessible from Firefox (this can’t be used by any other program,

or malicious software on your computer/local network).

These mappings are only functional when DevTools are opened.

You can register mappings from DevTools’ Options panel:

From there you can register as many mappings as you need.

The custom origin to expose via https URL.

The local folder where to load files from.

On the screenshot, it loads https://firefox.localhost from /home/alex/app .

When loading any file:// URL with DevTools opened, you should see the following notification

The first action Add To Settings will bring you to the Options panel and register

The second action Try it will register a transient mapping to load the current file or folder

from a https URL. The mapping will disappear as soon as you close DevTools or Firefox.

Mappings can also be managed in about:config via preferences, so that you can easily import and transfer them

Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Allow Remote Code Execution, Emergency Fixes Released
items.content:
The PHP development team has released emergency security updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected web servers. The fixes are available in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Administrators are strongly urged to upgrade immediately.

Both vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , carry a severity rating of 9.2 under CVSS 4.0. They affect PHP installations handling web requests, including those running PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.

According to the official PHP security advisory , the highest risk is associated with Apache’s mod_php configuration, where researchers have demonstrated that an unauthenticated request can trigger an attack before any application code executes.

The first vulnerability, CVE-2026-109618, involves memory corruption during out-of-memory handling. Under certain conditions, PHP can interrupt request processing while internal structures are only partially initialized, potentially causing subsequent cleanup operations to access invalid data.

The second, CVE-2026-109619, concerns stale global state. Memory belonging to a previous request can be freed while references to it remain accessible, allowing a later request handled by the same worker process to interact with invalid memory.

Importantly, exploiting these vulnerabilities does not require a vulnerable PHP application or a publicly accessible file-upload feature. The problems originate in PHP’s internal request processing, making them particularly concerning for administrators hosting otherwise properly maintained applications.

Debian has moved quickly to address the vulnerabilities. The project issued DSA-6574-1 , confirming that Debian 13 “Trixie” users can upgrade to PHP 8.4.27-1~deb13u1. Debian 12 “Bookworm” has received PHP 8.2.35-1~deb12u1 in its security repository, with both fixes explicitly listed in the package changelog.

The severity has also prompted an official warning from Arch Linux , which urges administrators running publicly accessible PHP applications to immediately upgrade to php 8.5.12 or php-legacy 8.3.36, depending on the installed package.

AlmaLinux technical steering committee has also approved releasing these fixes ahead of Red Hat and CentOS Stream. Patched packages are expected to reach testing repositories later today, followed by production repositories once testing is complete.

For other Linux distros, administrators should check their repositories for updated PHP packages. Distribution maintainers and long-term support vendors received the patches in advance to prepare security updates, including backported fixes where applicable.

PHP 8.1 and older versions are no longer supported by the upstream project, although some distributions may continue providing security patches. PHP 8.2, meanwhile, is approaching its end of life on December 31, 2026.

The PHP team also emphasizes that there are no complete workarounds for these vulnerabilities. Disabling session.upload_progress.enabled and restricting request sizes may reduce exposure to some attack paths, but these measures do not address every exploitation scenario.

Administrators should install the appropriate security update as soon as possible, and restart affected PHP workers or services to ensure the corrected code runs.

items.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
items.content:
New in OpenShell 0.1.x: a stable release cadence, new isolation primitives, an expanded extension surface, and new APIs. Read the 0.1.0 upgrade guide .

OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents. Agents are most useful when they can read files, install packages, call APIs, and use credentials. OpenShell gives them that capability without giving them unrestricted access to your data, secrets, or network. You declare what each agent can touch in a policy, and OpenShell enforces it.

OpenShell governs what agents can do in two ways: it instruments the kernel to enforce policy on every file access, system call, and network connection at runtime, and it uses formal verification to check what a policy change would allow before it is applied.

Kernel-level enforcement. Each agent runs in an isolated sandbox. Kernel controls confine which files it can access and which system calls it can make, and every network connection passes through a policy check before it leaves the sandbox. Agents never see real credentials; OpenShell adds them only to requests bound for approved endpoints.

Formally verified policy changes. Before a policy change is approved, OpenShell uses formal verification to flag risky new access it would grant, such as reaching a new host with credentials or calling a new API method, so those changes wait for human review.

See Architecture for how the gateway, supervisor, and sandbox fit together.

You need Linux, macOS on Apple Silicon, or Windows with WSL 2 (experimental), plus Docker, Podman, or host virtualization. See the Support Matrix for details.

curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/main/install.sh | sh

The installer sets up the CLI and a local gateway. The default sandbox image is minimal Ubuntu with no agent installed. To run a real agent, follow Run Your First Agent : it runs OpenCode against a free OpenRouter model and shows how to approve new access as the agent needs it.

Sandboxes : images, runtimes, GPUs, and lifecycle.

Policies : filesystem, network, and process rules, with the advisor and prover for reviewing changes.

Providers : credentials that work only at approved endpoints, including inference .

Gateways : the control plane for sandboxes, policy, and access.

Kubernetes : deploy the gateway with Helm. Your CNI must enforce NetworkPolicy .

Extensibility : middleware, interceptors, and compute drivers.

Tutorials : step-by-step policy and agent walkthroughs.

Prerelease and development builds : try an upcoming release or the latest commit on main .

Install the public OpenShell skills for your coding agent:

The skills teach your agent to drive the OpenShell CLI, write sandbox policies, and debug gateways and inference routing. They live in skills/ and work without an OpenShell source checkout.

SDKs connect applications to an OpenShell gateway. They do not install the CLI. Use the same OpenShell release for the SDK and the gateway when possible.

npm install @nvidia/openshell-sdk (GitHub Packages)

go get github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/sdk/go@latest

cargo add openshell-sdk --git https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell --tag <release-tag>

Questions and discussion: GitHub Discussions

Bug reports and feature requests: GitHub Issues , using the issue templates

Security vulnerabilities: follow SECURITY.md . Do not open a GitHub issue.

Roadmap: OpenShell Roadmap and the RFC board

OpenShell is built agent-first: it is developed with the same agent-driven workflows it enables. See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup and the contribution workflow, and AGENTS.md for repository coding conventions.

OpenShell collects anonymous telemetry, limited to operational categories and counts, to help improve the project. It does not collect sandbox names, hostnames, file paths, prompts, credentials, provider or model names, or user content. To disable it, set OPENSHELL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false on the gateway, or server.telemetryEnabled=false for Helm…

Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: Russian web brigades - Wikipedia
items.content:
Russian web brigades , [ a ] also called Russian trolls , Russian bots , RUbots, olgintsy , Kremlinbots , or Kremlin trolls , are state-sponsored anonymous Internet political commentators and trolls linked to the Russian government . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] Participants report that they are organized into teams and groups of commentators that participate in Russian and international political blogs and Internet forums using sockpuppets , social bots , and large-scale orchestrated trolling and disinformation campaigns to promote pro- Putin and pro- Russian propaganda , with an overtone of opposition to diversity, equity and inclusion , and of support for Russian imperialism . [ 1 ] [ 3 ] [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ]

Kremlin trolls are closely tied to the Internet Research Agency , a Saint Petersburg-based company run by Yevgeny Prigozhin , who was a close ally to Putin and head of the mercenary Wagner Group before his death in 2023. [ 7 ] Articles on the Russian Wikipedia concerning the MH17 crash and the Russo-Ukrainian War were targeted by Russian internet propaganda outlets. [ 1 ] [ 8 ] [ 9 ] [ 10 ] In June 2019, a group of 12 editors introducing coordinated pro-government and anti-opposition bias was blocked on the Russian-language Wikipedia. [ 11 ] During the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Kremlin trolls were still active on many social platforms and were spreading disinformation related to the war events . [ 12 ]

The earliest documented allegations of the existence of "web brigades" appear to be in the April 2003 Vestnik Online article "The Virtual Eye of Big Brother " by French journalist Anna Polyanskaya (a former assistant to assassinated Russian politician Galina Starovoitova [ 13 ] ) and two other authors, Andrey Krivov and Ivan Lomako. The authors claim that up to 1998, contributions to forums on Russian Internet sites ( Runet ) predominantly reflected liberal and democratic values, but after 2000, the vast majority of contributions reflected totalitarian values. This sudden change was attributed to the appearance of teams of pro-Russian commenters who appeared to be organized by the Russian state security service . [ 14 ] [ 15 ] [ 16 ] [ 17 ] According to the authors, about 70% of Russian Internet posters were of generally liberal views prior to 1998–1999, while a surge of "antidemocratic" posts (about 60–80%) suddenly occurred at many Russian forums in 2000. This could also be a reflection to the fact that access to Internet among the general Russian population soared during this time, which was until then accessible only to some sections of the society.

In January 2012, a hacktivist group calling itself the Russian arm of Anonymous published a massive collection of email allegedly belonging to former and present leaders of the pro-Putin youth organization Nashi (including a number of government officials). [ 18 ] Journalists who investigated the leaked information found that the pro-Putin movement had engaged in a range of activities including paying commentators to post content and hijacking blog ratings in the fall of 2011. [ 19 ] [ 20 ] The e-mails indicated that members of the "brigades" were paid 85 rubles (about US$3) or more per comment, depending on whether the comment received replies. Some were paid as much as 600,000 rubles (about US$21,000) for leaving hundreds of comments on negative press articles on the internet, and were presented with iPads. A number of high-profile bloggers were also mentioned as being paid for promoting Nashi and government activities. The Federal Youth Agency, whose head (and the former leader of Nashi) Vasily Yakemenko was the highest-ranking individual targeted by the leaks, refused to comment on the authenticity of the e-mails. [ 18 ] [ 21 ]

items.title: LiberNT: New ReactOS Fork Aims for Windows 11 Compatibility
items.content:
The LiberNT project is working on an alternative implementation of the Windows NT architecture, using Windows 11 version 24H2 as its compatibility reference. Unlike Linux distributions, LiberNT does not use the Linux kernel. It builds on the ReactOS codebase while replacing and extending several core components.

One of the project’s main priorities is ARM64 support, particularly for single-board computers and embedded devices. LiberNT also supports x86-64 and 32-bit x86, while RISC-V 64-bit and PowerPC ports are under development.

According to the developers, the implementation follows a clean-room approach. Windows behavior is studied using Microsoft’s public documentation, SDK and WDK headers, public symbols, and black-box testing. The team states no proprietary Windows code is copied or transcribed.

On the technical side, one of the biggest changes is NVS, a new memory manager and kernel pool implementation replacing the corresponding ReactOS components. LiberNT also introduces a new cache manager, with developers claiming better results than the original ReactOS memory manager in their memory and cache benchmarks.

Other changes include a new NTFS driver, an updated StorPort implementation with NVMe support, USB xHCI and SD bus drivers, and work on the Windows Display Driver Model and Desktop Window Manager.

On the application compatibility side, LiberNT implements WoW64 on its 64-bit targets, while ARM64 systems use the FEX emulator to run x86 applications. ARM64EC support is also part of the project.

Early compatibility results are already available on the project’s compatibility page . According to tests published by the developers, Google Chrome, the open-source strategy game 0 A.D., and Command & Conquer: Yuri’s Revenge are reported to work. Steam is listed as usable, while the RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator currently starts but has not been classified as usable.

However, the compatibility database contains only five entries, all tested against a specific development build.

LiberNT also targets Raspberry Pi hardware, with the same ARM64 disk image designed to boot on Raspberry Pi 3, Raspberry Pi 5, and generic ARM64 virtual machines running under QEMU. The project includes drivers for Raspberry Pi display, networking, and audio hardware.

For those interested in trying it, the developers provide downloadable builds in three formats: a preinstalled raw disk image, a VHD image for virtualization platforms, and a bootable installation ISO. The preinstalled image is recommended, with support for both UEFI and BIOS booting.

Still, LiberNT remains a work in progress. The developers caution that the available builds are experimental and should be used in virtual machines or on spare hardware rather than production systems. The source code is available on GitHub .

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.
